nodes.title: Price of anarchy 5/2 for no-regret play in affine congestion games

nodes.summary: Let a congestion game have affine delays $d_e(n) = a_e n + b_e$ with $a_e, b_e \ge 0$. Then for all profiles $s$ and $t$, where $C$ is the social cost: the game is $(5/3, 1/3)$-smooth.
nodes.title: Affine congestion games are (5/3, 1/3)-smooth

nodes.summary: In a congestion game, if player $i$ switches from $s_i$ to any strategy $a$, the load of every resource increases by at most one: $n_e(a, s_{-i}) \le n_e(s) + 1$.
nodes.title: Load after a unilateral deviation

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $y$ and $z$, Equality holds at $(y, z) = (1, 1)$ and $(1, 2)$. The inequality fails for real numbers, e.g. at $y = 1/2$, $z = 1$: integrality of the loads is what makes the atomic bound $5/2$ differ from the nonatomic $4/3$.
nodes.title: Christodoulou–Koutsoupias inequality

nodes.summary: In a congestion game with affine delays $d_e(n) = a_e n + b_e$, $a_e, b_e \ge 0$, every pure Nash equilibrium $s$ satisfies $C(s) \le \tfrac52\, C(t)$ for every profile $t$. The bound $5/2$ is tight.
